# 1 Samuel Chapter 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 167r–168r | **Source Image:** 1SA_030_page_001.jpg, 1SA_030_page_002.jpg, 1SA_030_page_003.jpg

---

**30:1** And-it-was when-David and-his-men came to-Ziklag on-the-third day, and-[the]-Amalekites had-raided the-Negev and-Ziklag, and-they-struck Ziklag and-burned it with-fire.

**30:2** And-they-captured the-women who [were]-in-it, from-small unto-great; they-did-not put-to-death anyone, but-drove [them] and-went on-their-way.

**30:3** And-came David and-his-men to-the-city, and-behold, [it was]-burned with-fire, and-their-wives and-their-sons and-their-daughters had-been-taken-captive.

**30:4** And-David and-the-people who [were]-with-him lifted-up their-voice and-wept until there-was-no strength in-them to-weep.

**30:5** And-[the]-two wives of-David had-been-taken-captive: Ahinoam the-Jezreelitess and-Abigail [the]-wife of-Nabal the-Carmelite.

**30:6** And-it-was-distressing to-David exceedingly, for the-people spoke of-stoning-him, for [the]-soul of-all the-people was-bitter, each over his-sons and-over his-daughters. And-David strengthened-himself in-YHWH his-God.

**30:7** And-said David to-Abiathar the-priest, son of-Ahimelech, "Bring-near, please, to-me the-ephod." And-Abiathar brought-near the-ephod to-David.

**30:8** And-inquired David of-YHWH, saying, "Shall-I-pursue after this raiding-band? Shall-I-overtake-it?" And-He-said to-him, "Pursue, for you-shall-surely overtake and-you-shall-surely deliver."

**30:9** And-went David, he and-six-hundred men who [were]-with-him, and-they-came to-[the]-brook of-Besor, and-the-remaining-ones stood.

**30:10** And-pursued David, he and-four-hundred men, and-stood two-hundred men who were-too-exhausted to-cross [the]-brook of-Besor.

**30:11** And-they-found an-Egyptian man in-the-field and-took him to-David, and-gave to-him bread and-he-ate, and-gave-him-to-drink water.

**30:12** And-they-gave to-him a-piece of-a-cake-of-figs and-two cakes-of-raisins, and-he-ate, and-his-spirit returned to-him, for he-had-not eaten bread and-had-not drunk water three days and-three nights.

**30:13** And-said to-him David, "To-whom [do]-you [belong], and-from-where [are]-you?" And-he-said, "A-young-man, an-Egyptian [am]-I, servant of-a-man, an-Amalekite. And-my-master abandoned-me because I-was-sick three days ago.

**30:14** We raided the-Negev of-the-Cherethites and-that which [is]-to-Judah and-the-Negev of-Caleb, and-Ziklag we-burned with-fire."

**30:15** And-said to-him David, "Will-you-bring-me-down to this raiding-band?" And-he-said, "Swear to-me by-God that you-will-not put-me-to-death and-that you-will-not deliver-me into-[the]-hand of-my-master, and-I-will-bring-you-down to this raiding-band."

**30:16** And-he-brought-him-down, and-behold, they [were]-spread-out over-[the]-face of-all the-land, eating and-drinking and-feasting [chogegim] with-all the-great spoil which they-had-taken from-[the]-land of-[the]-Philistines and-from-[the]-land of-Judah.

**30:17** And-struck-them David from-the-twilight [ha-neshef] and-until the-evening of-the-next-day. And-not-a-man of-them escaped, except four-hundred young men who rode upon the-camels and-fled.

**30:18** And-David recovered all that [the]-Amalekites had-taken, and-his-two wives David rescued.

**30:19** And-nothing was-missing for-them, from-small and-unto great, and-unto sons and-daughters, and-from-spoil and-unto all that they-had-taken for-themselves; the-whole David brought-back.

**30:20** And-took David all the-flocks and-the-herds; they-drove before that livestock and-said, "This [is the]-spoil of-David."

**30:21** And-came David to the-two-hundred men who had-been-too-exhausted to-go after-David, and-they-had-made-them-sit at-[the]-brook of-Besor. And-they-went-out to-meet David and-to-meet the-people who [were]-with-him. And-drew-near David to-the-people and-asked them of-welfare [shalom].

**30:22** And-answered every evil and-worthless man [ish beliya'al] from-the-men who went with-David and-said, "Because they-did-not go with-us, we-will-not give to-them from-the-spoil which we-recovered, except each his-wife and-his-children; let-them-drive [them] and-go."

**30:23** And-said David, "You-shall-not do so, my-brothers, with-that-which YHWH has-given to-us, and-He-guarded us and-gave the-raiding-band that-came against-us into-our-hand.

**30:24** And-who will-listen to-you in-this matter? For as-the-share of-the-[one]-going-down into-the-battle, so [shall be]-the-share of-the-[one]-staying by-the-vessels; together they-shall-share."

**30:25** And-it-was from-that day and-onward, and-he-set-it [as]-a-statute and-[as]-an-ordinance for-Israel until this day.

**30:26** And-came David to-Ziklag and-sent from-the-spoil to-[the]-elders of-Judah, to-his-friends, saying, "Behold, a-blessing for-you from-[the]-spoil of-[the]-enemies of-YHWH":

**30:27** to-those in-Beth-el, and-to-those in-Ramoth of-the-Negev, and-to-those in-Jattir,

**30:28** and-to-those in-Aroer, and-to-those in-Siphmoth, and-to-those in-Eshtemoa,

**30:29** and-to-those in-Racal, and-to-those in-the-cities of-the-Jerahmeelites, and-to-those in-the-cities of-the-Kenites,

**30:30** and-to-those in-Hormah, and-to-those in-Bor-ashan, and-to-those in-Athach,

**30:31** and-to-those in-Hebron, and-to-all the-places where David had-walked-about, he and-his-men.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **30:6 — "David strengthened himself in YHWH his God"**: The pivotal moment — abandoned, bereaved, threatened with stoning by his own men, David turns to YHWH. This contrasts with Saul's response to crisis (consulting the medium at En-dor, ch.28).

2. **30:14 — Cherethites**: Often identified with Cretans or a Philistine subgroup. They later form part of David's royal bodyguard (2 Sam 8:18).

3. **30:24-25 — Spoil-sharing ordinance**: David establishes a lasting principle of equal distribution. This act of legislation shows David already functioning as a lawgiver-king.

4. **30:26-31 — Distribution list**: David sends gifts to Judean towns where he found refuge. This is political strategy — building alliances in advance of his kingship over Judah (2 Sam 2:4).

— EMET
